verdict.verdict:
v2 is not worse than v1 before the panel-of-normals (PoN) filter, and modestly worse after it. The big gap the user remembers comes from a v1 design whose graph contains the patient's own normal genome, not from the .dat/.idx tensor format.

Comparison basis: same 697 chr1 PASS SNP truths, same somatic BED ∩ germline BED, strict allele matching, false calls counted once per distinct GRCh38 allele. Model versions compared: the published v1 SNV model (byte-identical to model_e067 of the pasted AF-HPRC run, graph without HG008-N) and its sibling checkpoint e053 (the only one with real chr1 VCFs on this server), against the four v2 runs.

(a) No PoN: essentially a tie.
- v2 wins at low recall. Recall at precision 0.15 is 0.49-0.61 for v2 against ≤0.01 for v1. Max F1 is 0.255-0.281 for v2 against 0.183 for v1 e053 (exact) and 0.190 [0.182-0.202] for v1 e067 (estimate).
- v1 is slightly better at high recall. At the same TP 608 (recall 0.872), precision is 0.100 for v1 against 0.096 (allnon), 0.093 (keephard) and 0.077 (base).
- Neither model rejects the patient's germline SNPs that are missing from the graph: 5,341 germline false calls for v1 against 5,020-5,264 for v2.

(b) After the same repo-rule PoN: v1 is ahead.
- At TP 561 (recall 0.805), precision is 0.522 for v1 (its own PoN VCF) against 0.463 (allnon), 0.431 (keephard) and 0.334 (base).
- Max F1 is 0.643-0.656 for v1 e053 and about 0.672 [0.649-0.701] for v1 e067 (estimate), against 0.623 (keephard), 0.618 (allnon) and 0.528 (base).
- The whole post-PoN gap is non-germline, mostly low-AF noise. At TP 608, v1 has 105 non-germline false calls; v2 has 563-2,276.
- This ranking depends on the PoN rule. With an AF ≥0.001 rule the two tie (v1 0.508, v2 0.471-0.526).

The dramatic 'old design' numbers belong to AF_HPRC_HG008N_added: P 0.89, R 0.874, 75 false calls; per-tensor F1 0.7757. That graph has HG008-N's own 5.2 M dipcall variants injected, which amounts to using a matched normal, so it is not a valid tumor-only baseline.

What is still open:
- The exact v1 e067 curve. The current one is a stratified-sample estimate. A GPU inference run with no training (head_to_head/run_v1_full_gpu.sh, estimated under 30 min per checkpoint) would make it exact. The sample's confidence interval already puts v1 ahead after PoN, apart from the unknown optimism from choosing v1's epoch on chr1.
- Why v2 lets more low-AF noise through. The strongest candidate is v2's partial-match positive labels (untested hypothesis). Settling it takes one GPU retraining ablation of about 3 h (keephard config: 840 s/epoch × 12).

why_v1_looks_better: 1. The best 'v1' numbers used the patient's normal (largest effect). Tensor F1 0.7757 and truth-level P 0.89 / R 0.874 come from AF_HPRC_HG008N_added. Its graph is d9 plus HG008-N's own dipcall variants: /scratch/jshen/Scripts/HG008_GIAB/add_hg008n_to_hprc-af_vg.sh runs dipcall on HG008N_curatedv6 hap1/hap2, then vg convert -p -H, then vg add (5,221,087 variants, the same VCF body as v2's germline truth). That removes the germline false calls (9 against 5,341) and amounts to a matched normal. The pasted/published model is NOT this design: its 106 training shards and 3,116,015 samples match AF_HPRC, and its first 8 validation shards give exactly 261,620 / 524.

2. v1 is quoted after PoN, v2 before it (large effect). v1 e053 + PoN scores F1 0.633 strict (0.622 in the user's rtg run); v2 without PoN peaks at max F1 0.26-0.28. Both models carry about 5,000-5,300 germline false calls at R 0.872, and the PoN removes about 90% of them. With the same PoN on both, the gap shrinks to 0.02-0.13 F1 (v1 0.643-0.672 against v2 0.528-0.623).

3. Different metric and denominator. The pasted 'P 9.86% at R 93.5%' is per tensor, over 524 true tensors in the first 8 of 11 chr1 validation shards, with the epoch picked on that same set. On that metric v2 gets 0.064-0.092 against v1's 0.0986 (0.106 when v1 e067 is re-run on CPU). This is a real but modest v1 advantage, about 10-40% lower precision for v2 at R 0.935. It exists only at the very-high-recall end.

4. v1's epoch was selected on chr1; v2 never saw chr1. Probably small (hypothesis): v1 validation F1 moved only 0.169 → 0.178 between epochs 24 and 67, and truth-level max F1 is 0.183 for e053 against 0.190 for e067.
5. The user's own evaluations used no BED and a 702-record baseline (rtg --region chr1). Small effect: v1 e053 + PoN gets rtg F1 0.622 against 0.633 strict in-BED.

6. v2's built-in test metrics count off-reference tensors as non (EVAL_AS_NON), while v1's linear VCF drops them. This lowers v2 base max F1 from 0.260 to 0.242. They cannot be false positives against a GRCh38 truth, so they belong in a separate graph-VCF evaluation. Small to moderate for base and allnon.
real_design_differences: 1. Positive labels (most likely cause; hypothesis consistent with the numbers). v2 labels residual partial matches as somatic: on chr2-22, 2,156 of 9,768 label-1 SNV tensors, median AF 0.126, 1,473 of them with AF <0.2. That makes 97% of all v2 positives with AF <0.2 partial matches (exact ones: 46 of 7,612). v1 labels only exact matches: 7,634 true, and on chr1 validation 2 of 670 have AF <0.2. The failure has the same signature: after PoN, 913 of v2's 1,196 non-germline false calls have AF <0.2, against 13 for v1. At TP 608, v2 has 563-2,276 non-germline false calls against 105 for v1. Also, 952 of those v2 false calls are v1 candidates that v1 scored below 0.5. Sources: synthesis/pos_af.out, v1_artifacts/fp_comp2.out, synthesis/my_check.out.

2. Training schedule (medium). v2 ran 12 epochs at lr 2e-4 with 1 warmup epoch. Base and keephard peak at epoch 5 and then overfit (base val loss 0.097 → 0.335), with non tensors subsampled to 25% per epoch (about 4-5 M tensor passes to the best epoch). v1 ran 80 epochs at lr 1e-4 with 10 warmup epochs and cosine decay, on 90% of shards per epoch (about 188 M passes to e067). Exposure alone is not the fix: allnon_w100 (all non every epoch) still has 563 non-germline false calls at TP 608, and its validation truth F1 plateaus at 0.22-0.24 from epoch 2.

3. Which negatives are trained (medium-low). v2 marks out-of-BED tensors -1 (92,336 on chr1), and off-reference tensors never train. v1 trains on every false tensor, including out-of-BED ones (95,871 on chr1 validation). v2 calls 91-1,216 of 10,295 off-reference tensors at p ≥0.5; v1 calls 19 of 16,018.

4. Row selection and encoding (unknown impact; hypothesis). v1 sorts reads with the most mismatches first before the 200-row cap, and has an explicit mismatch-flag channel across the 100-column window (5 at the variant column), so a read's mismatch burden is visible directly. v2 samples rows uniformly within allele blocks, orders them by similarity, and marks alleles in site_allele; mismatches must be inferred from read_base against the graph reference base.

5. AF floor (low). v2 builds at 0.06 and labels at 0.07; v1 uses 0.08. 215 of v2's 1,196 post-PoN non-germline false calls are not v1 candidates. Restricting v2 to AF ≥0.08 adds only 0.01-0.03 to max F1 (h2h).

6. Germline class / 3 classes (low; neither helps nor provably hurts). At TP 608, v2's germline false calls are 5,020-5,264 against v1's 5,341, a reduction of 6% at most. Tumor-only tensors cannot tell a private germline het from a clonal somatic variant (AF medians 0.60 and 0.55). The class only buys v2's higher-precision points at low recall.

7. Class weights (low). v2 base uses somatic weight 5.6, keephard/allnon 100, v1 200. A v2 run with weights 1/200/10 on all non tensors (HG008_Illumina_SNV_allnon_w1_200_10_b512_fixed) was worse on validation (truth F1 ≤0.16) and was cancelled at epoch 11 (job 377155).

8. Not a difference: graph and population information. Both use the plain d9 graph with no gnomAD channel; v1's genomead_af JSON field is not read by the 5-channel builder. Candidate ceilings are the same (660 against 659 exact alleles; the same 660 truths). v2's extra channels (strand, graph reference base, a near-constant path count) are not implicated.
next_steps: 1. Free: ask the user which v1 number they are comparing against. If it is F1 0.78 per tensor, or P 0.89-0.96 at truth level, it is the HG008N_added (patient-normal) design and cannot serve as a tumor-only baseline. From now on, report every v1 and v2 result with the same PoN post-filter and the same truth-level scorer (synthesis/my_check.py or head_to_head/h2h_final.py).

2. CPU, under 15 min, read-only: characterize the 952 low-AF v2 false calls that v1 scores below 0.5 against v2's true positives. Check ALT-strand fraction, ALT base quality, MAPQ, per-read mismatch burden, distance to the nearest somatic INDEL truth, and whether the site resembles v2's partial-match training positives. This shows which ablation to run first.

3. GPU inference, no training, estimated under 30 min per checkpoint (needs user approval): head_to_head/run_v1_full_gpu.sh (v1_full_chr1_gpu_test.py plus score_v1_full.py) on all 361,394 v1 chr1 test tensors, for e067 and e053. This turns the v1 e067 estimate into an exact curve at every threshold, including P@R0.9 and off-reference calls. Copy the scratch scripts somewhere persistent first.

4. GPU training, about 3 h (keephard_w100 config, 840 s/epoch × 12): relabel residual_partial_somatic_truth (and allele_partial) SNV tensors to -1, then retrain on chr2-22 and test on chr1. Success criterion: non-germline false calls at TP 608 fall from 695 toward about 105, and post-PoN precision at R 0.805 reaches ≥0.52 (v1's level).

5. Only if step 4 is not enough, one change at a time: SNV label floor 0.08; lr 1e-4 with a longer warmup and cosine schedule; out-of-BED and off-reference non tensors added to training as negatives; v1-like mismatch-first row ordering, or a per-read mismatch-count plane.
6. For future fair comparisons, select v1 checkpoints on a non-chr1 validation set, or state that v1's chr1 numbers carry some optimism from epoch selection on chr1.

investigations.summary:
Scratch dir: analysis/v1_vs_v2_20260929/v1_artifacts/. Scripts: v1_verify.py, count_labels2.py, germ_af.py, fp_comp2.py. Outputs: the matching .out files and ckpt_keys.out. Everything ran read-only on CPU; the largest run took 80 s and about 1.1 GB. An earlier, unfinished run of this same task left v1_eval.out and old_src/ here. I reused them after checking them against the new tensor paths.

**Short answer.** There were two v1 designs, and they must not be mixed up.
- **v1 "AF_HPRC" (the design without a normal).** This is the pasted run and the published HG008_WGS_SNV.pth. On the same 697 truths it is about as good as v2 before the PoN filter, and better than v2 after it.
- **v1 "AF_HPRC_HG008N_added".** Its graph contains the patient's own normal assembly, which amounts to using a matched normal. It is the only v1 design with very good numbers.

**(1) Graph**
- AF_HPRC is the plain HPRC v1.1 MC GRCh38 d9 graph (hprc-v1.1-mc-grch38.d9.gbz). The Zenodo readme calls this the "AF-filtered" graph: nodes carried by fewer than 10% of haplotypes are removed. Nothing is added to it: no gnomAD, no HG008-N.
- AF_HPRC_HG008N_added is that d9 graph with the HG008-N dipcall variants injected by `vg add` (5,221,087 variants), then rebuilt by autoindex with the haplotypes dropped and a greedy path-cover GBWT. Its variant set is byte-identical to v2's germline truth VCF.
- The pasted run used AF_HPRC. Its shard and sample counts (106/11 shards, 3,116,015 training tensors, 261,620/524 validation) match AF_HPRC exactly. They do not match HG008N_added (95/9 shards, 2,679,647 training tensors, first 8 validation shards = 261,533/611).
- The published HG008_WGS_SNV.pth is byte-identical to that run's model_e067_f1_0.1784.pth.

**(2) Candidates**
- Nodes go into the .dat when more than 5% of their mappings are imperfect. Reads need MAPQ ≥10.
- SNV edits come from the CIGAR against the node sequence. Filters: at least 3 ALT reads, AF ≥0.08, mean ALT base quality ≥10.
- One tensor is made per (node, offset, ALT). Training and validation use GRCh38-path nodes only; the test set adds the component's non-reference nodes (+16,018 tensors on chr1).
- There is no population-AF filter. The `genomead_af` arrays in the ref_nodes_position JSONs are not read by the 5-channel builder.
- In principle this is the same kind of candidate as v2 (edits against the walked node), so germline variants already in d9 are never candidates.

**(3) Labels**
- "true" means an exact (position, REF, ALT) match to HG008-T_somatic_smvar_benchmark_v0.2_tumorvariants.snv.vcf.gz: 9,609 records, all FILTER '.', 702 on chr1. Because of the fetch window, a truth one base downstream with the same REF/ALT also counts.
- No BED is used, either for labels or in the user's rtg evaluations (`vcfeval --region chr1`).
- Germline variants that are candidates are labelled "false". On chr1 validation that is 23,697 of the false tensors; in chr2-22 training it is 310,031 germline false against 7,634 true (40.6:1).

**(4) Channels.** Five int8 channels of shape (5, 201, 100): row 0 is the node's reference sequence, then up to 200 reads.
- base (A20 C30 G50 T70 N5 *1 I90, padding 0)
- base quality
- mismatch flag (0/1, 5 at the variant column, padding -1)
- MAPQ (padding -1)
- CIGAR op (M10 … X90)

There is no strand channel and no population AF. Reads are sorted with mismatch-heavy reads first before the 200-row cap.

**(5) Counts**
- AF_HPRC chr1 validation: 345,376 tensors = 344,706 false + 670 true (11 shards). The pasted 261,620/524 is exactly the running total after shards 00000-00007 (262,144 = 8 × 32,768). Why the log says 11 shards but evaluated 8 is not explained.
- AF_HPRC chr2-22 training: 3,108,381 false + 7,634 true.
- Ceilings on the 697 truths: AF_HPRC 660 (0.947, the same 660 that v2 has as tensor_representative); HG008N_added 669 (0.960); v2 662 (0.950).

**(6) Existing v1 chr1 predictions.** These are VCFs holding only calls with PROB ≥0.5 (argmax), so only the high-threshold end of a curve exists. None of them comes from the published e067 checkpoint; the AF_HPRC ones come from e053 (also selected on chr1). Strict scoring on the 697 truths, with FP counted as distinct alleles inside somatic BED ∩ germline BED:

| Model / filter | P | R | F1 | FP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AF_HPRC e053 | 0.100 | 0.872 | 0.180 | 5,446 (5,341 of them HG008-N germline) |
| AF_HPRC e053 + 4-PoN | 0.522 | 0.805 | 0.633 | 514 |
| HG008N_added e064 | 0.890 | 0.874 | 0.882 | 75 |
| HG008N_added e064 + 4-PoN | 0.959 | 0.806 | 0.876 | 24 |

**Why v2 looks worse (matched recall 0.872, TP 608 for both).**
- The germline false-positive load is about the same: v1 e053 5,341 against v2 base 5,020.
- The non-germline false positives differ a lot: v1 105, v2 2,277.
- After the PoN filter: v1 514 (55 non-germline) against v2 1,616 (1,196 non-germline).
- 76% of v2's remaining non-germline false positives have AF <0.2. 952 of them are v1 candidates that v1 scored below 0.5. So v2 is mostly worse at rejecting low-AF noise, not at rejecting germline.
- A likely cause is v2's partial-match positives (median AF 0.12). That is a hypothesis, not tested here.

**Needs a GPU.** A full v1 curve for the published e067 checkpoint on chr1 (about 361k tensors).

investigations.summary:
**Verdict.** On the same 697 chr1 truths and the same region (somatic BED ∩ germline BED), v2 is not worse than v1 before the panel-of-normals (PoN) filter. The two are equally poor: precision is about 0.10–0.11 at recall 0.8–0.9. After the PoN filter that the v1 pipeline used, v1 is modestly better: max F1 0.672 against 0.625 for the best v2 run and 0.535 for v2 base. The gap widens when v2's off-reference false calls are counted. The very good "old design" numbers the user may remember (tensor F1 0.78, truth F1 0.88–0.90) come from the HG008N_added graph, which contains the patient's own normal genome. That is equivalent to using a matched normal.

facts.claim: Hypotheses for why v2 rejects non-germline noise worse than v1, not tested here: (a) the residual partial-match somatic labels (188 of 852 on chr1; 22% genome-wide) are low-AF, noise-like positives; (b) the short, subsampled training (about 10 M passes against about 224 M), with overfitting after epoch 5; (c) the 3-class setup, with germline outnumbering somatic about 30:1; (d) off-reference tensors are never trained on in either design, but v2 generalizes worse to them (1,216 calls ≥ 0.5 for keephard against 19 for v1).

needs_gpu_or_user: The exact v1 e067 curve at every threshold, including off-reference candidates (the numbers here are a stratified-sample estimate with 95% intervals, plus the exact e053 curve above 0.5). Run sbatch analysis/v1_vs_v2_20260929/head_to_head/run_v1_full_gpu.sh (not submitted). It runs v1_full_chr1_gpu_test.py for the published checkpoint (e067) and for e053 on all 361,394 tensors in /scratch/jshen/data/Pansoma/HG008_GIAB/AF_HPRC/5ch_testing_data_SNV/5ch_testing_data_SNV_chr1/shard_000{00..11}_data.npy, then score_v1_full.py (tested by re-deriving the e053 VCF results). Expect well under 30 min per checkpoint on one GPU, reading about 36 GB each; on CPU it would be about 12 h per checkpoint. Copy the scratch dir somewhere persistent first.

Unexplained: in the pasted training log the trainer evaluated only 262,144 of the 345,376 val rows (the first 8 of 11 shards), and on CPU the published model finds 484 of 524 true tensors where the log reports 490. Probably not decisive.

A design decision for the user (not a measurement): v2 already matches or beats v1 before the PoN filter. The remaining gap after PoN is v2's non-germline false positives (on-reference label-0 and off-reference tensors), not germline. Ablations to test the hypotheses: (1) train with the partial-match somatic labels removed or set to -1; (2) train longer, or without subsampling non tensors at 25%; (3) add off-reference non tensors to training. Each needs GPU training.
